profile.campus: Hillsboro, Oregon (Flexential's Hillsboro data center campus, four existing buildings plus a fifth completed and a sixth planned as of 2025)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 5) is located at 4975 NE Starr Blvd, Hillsboro, OR 97124. The operator publishes a footprint of 358000 square feet and 36 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including HITRUST CSF, PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building is part of Flexential's wider Hillsboro campus, which Data Center Dynamics reported in 2025 had grown to five sites (four existing buildings plus Hillsboro 5, then under construction) totaling 1.18 million square feet and 113 megawatts of capacity, with a sixth facility then being planned across from Hillsboro 1 at 350,000 square feet and 27 megawatts. Flexential president and COO Ryan Mallory described Hillsboro as "a smart alternative to Silicon Valley for customers seeking the performance, flexibility, and cost structure they can't find elsewhere, especially those with strong ties across the Pacific." DCD also reported that the Hillsboro market ran extremely tight in the first half of 2025, with a vacancy rate of just 0.2% and 48.4 megawatts of absorption against 48 megawatts of new supply delivered, roughly 10% of total market inventory turning over in six months. Hillsboro sits in Oregon's "Silicon Forest" technology corridor west of Portland, built up around Intel's long-standing local manufacturing presence and the skilled workforce it created, a legacy that has also drawn other major data center operators, including Meta, to the same area.

The City of Hillsboro reports that, as of July 2026, the city hosted 23 total data center sites, 16 already constructed across 346 acres plus 7 more in permitting or under construction across another 224 acres, together occupying roughly 570 of the city's 17,378 total acres. In 2025, Hillsboro's data center sector generated about $61.1 million in total taxes; 12 entities receiving Enterprise Zone property-tax abatements held roughly $7.2 billion in exempted real market value, out of an $11 billion combined assessed/exempted value across all data centers in the city. Eligible facilities receive temporary property-tax abatement on new investment for three to five years under Hillsboro's Enterprise Zone program, after which standard property taxes apply, alongside application fees capped at $50,000 and Community Service Fees of up to 33% of abated taxes in the first three years. Statewide, Oregon's data center industry supported an estimated 9,310 direct jobs and 38,380 indirect and induced jobs, with more than $4.1 billion in labor income, in 2023, according to industry analysis cited by the city.

reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 5 publishes 36 MW of critical load UPS capacity across 358,000 square feet in Hillsboro, Oregon. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, this IT load would support roughly 900 racks. The facility holds NIST 800-53, ITAR, and SOC 2 Type II certifications, qualifying it to host sensitive federal and financial computing.

This campus ranks first by published megawatts among eight facilities with disclosed capacity in Oregon, and represents 23 percent of the state's published total of 156.6 MW. Oregon has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, but only eight have published power figures, making disclosed capacity rare in the state's footprint.

The campus matters to AI scaling if Oregon becomes a meaningful power source for accelerator workloads, which depends on whether Flexential chooses to market this facility to cloud AI providers and whether the regional grid can support significant incremental load. Neither fact is published.
